extracted.intended_audience: war correspondents, news editors and the general reading public
extracted.subtask_description: A set of voluntary press-security rules and reporting guidance for journalists covering active military operations (here, the Korean War), advising what operational details to withhold and how to phrase unit references to protect personnel and operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary press code to ensure operational security
rubrics_metrics.description: General exhortation from General MacArthur that the press should establish a voluntary code to ensure the security of operations and the safety of personnel by preventing detrimental information being made available to hostile forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MacArthur 'does not desire to invoke censorship' and 'prefers that the press establish a voluntary code' that will prevent publication of information which could endanger lives or operations. The press is asked to accept responsibility for security-conscious reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not report troop movements (proposed or in progress)
rubrics_metrics.description: DO NOT REPORT MOVEMENTS, PROPOSED OR IN PROGRESS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit rule: avoid reporting actual troop movements, whether planned or underway, because such reporting 'endangers our interests and the lives of our soldiers, sailors and airmen engaged in combat.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not name locations of units, air bases or headquarters
rubrics_metrics.description: DO NOT NAME LOCATIONS OF UNITS, AIR BASES, HEADQUARTERS OR ... (locations and troop movements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid publishing specific locations of units, airfields, headquarters or other operational sites. This includes places of landings and undisclosed movement destinations; such details should not be reported while operations are underway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not publish specific unit identifiers, sizes, titles or landing details
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports naming specific units, sizes, titles, places of landings, locations and troop movements as well as vilification of our armed forces should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from publishing unit designations, strengths, precise titles, or details about landings/first units until officially released; avoid sensationalizing or vilifying friendly forces. These specifics can materially assist hostile forces if disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer only to major units; use generic phrasing for smaller units
rubrics_metrics.description: REFER ONLY TO MAJOR UNITS: FIFTH AIR FORCE, TWENTIETH AIR FORCE, EIGHTH ARMY AND SEVENTH FLEET AFTER OFFICIAL ANNOUNCEMENT OF THEIR COMMITMENT. FOR SMALLER UNITS USE SUCH EXPRESSIONS AS 'UNITS FROM THE EIGHTH ARMY,' 'UNITS FROM THE TWENTIETH AIR FORCE,' 'TASK FORCE FROM THE SEVENTH FLEET.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only name large formations (and only after official confirmation of their commitment). For smaller formations use broad, non-identifying terms to avoid revealing force structure or deployments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep in mind the telephone is not secure
rubrics_metrics.description: KEEP IN MIND AT ALL TIMES THAT THE TELEPHONE IS NOT SECURE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume telephonic channels and other ad hoc communications from the field can be intercepted; avoid transmitting sensitive operational details via insecure lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security consciousness must start at the source and continue through publication
rubrics_metrics.description: SECURITY CONSCIOUSNESS MUST START AT THE SOURCE, WITH THE CORRESPONDENTS IN THE FIELD, AND CONTINUE THROUGH TO THE END.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters, signal corps, telephone employees and editors should all exercise caution. Security awareness should be maintained from initial field reporting through editing and publication so that inadvertent disclosures are prevented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inaccurate or irresponsible reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The release asserts that inaccurate and irresponsible reporting endangers interests and lives and that a responsible press will avoid such reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize verification and restraint; do not publish unconfirmed frontline claims or sensational, unverified victory claims. Accuracy and responsibility are framed as ethical obligations tied to personnel safety.
